prompt_package.goal_summary: Make one ad image per language with the same layout, so a campaign looks identical in every market.

user_profile.who: Marketer or freelancer running a small international campaign
user_profile.language: English (output can be any language the model supports)

blocks.task: Create a social ad for {{brand}} in {{language}}. Same layout as the attached master image. Only the headline and the small print change language.
blocks.subject: {{product}} placed on the {{position}} of the frame. A {{brand_color}} shape sits behind it. The {{text_zone}} third is left empty for type.
blocks.scene: Clean {{background_color}} backdrop, one soft shadow, no props. Layout identical to the reference: same margins, same logo position at {{logo_position}}, same text alignment.
blocks.camera: Straight-on product view, no perspective. Layout matches the reference image pixel for pixel.
blocks.light: Even soft studio light from above, gentle contact shadow, no visible light source.

text_in_image.placement: {{text_zone}} third, centered horizontally in that zone
text_in_image.size: two lines maximum, about 18% of frame height per line

text_in_image.style: medium weight, same color at 80% opacity
text_in_image.size: about one third of the headline size

locks: Layout, margins, logo position and product placement match the master image exactly.
Write the text in {{language}}. Use the correct characters and accents for that language.
Copy each string exactly as given. Do not translate, shorten or add words.
avoid: mixing two languages in one image
decorative shapes that move the logo

input_schema.description: One JSON file per language. Everything except language, headline, subline and legal line stays the same.

fields.name: headline
fields.example: ÁGUA FRIA ATÉ O FIM DO DIA

output_schema.description: One image per language, plus a check that nothing moved.

fields.name: layout_hash_check
fields.example: Stack the language versions in one file. Logo and product must sit at the same pixels.

example_input.headline: ÁGUA FRIA ATÉ O FIM DO DIA

example_output.layout_hash_check: Logo matches master at top left; accents on Á and á correct.
Text zone unchanged; headline reflows to one line.

non_obvious_insights: Make the first language the master image, then attach it as a reference for every other language. Text alignment stops drifting.
Line length is the real enemy. German and Portuguese run longer than English; write the shortest version first and translate up.
Never ask the model to translate. You supply native copy. The model's job is drawing, not localization.
Some scripts need more line height. Expect Japanese and Thai to need a shorter headline, not a smaller font.
Say 'do not translate, do not shorten'. Without that line the model quietly rewrites your copy.
Check accents at 100% zoom. Missing diacritics are the most common defect and the easiest to miss.
Two languages in one image almost always means mixed glyphs. One image per language, always.
monetization_ideas: Sell 'one campaign, five markets' as a flat package to exporters.
Charge per language variant, not per hour: it scales with client value.
Offer a quarterly refresh: same layout, new offer, every market.
Partner with translation freelancers: they supply copy, you supply images, you split the job.
Sell the master image plus the JSON as a brand asset kit so in-house teams can self-serve.
prompt_package.reusability_notes: Swap language, headline and legal line to add markets. Change aspect_ratio to 9:16 for stories or 1:1 for feeds; the layout locks hold. For a new product, keep the master and change only product and background color; for a new offer, change only the headline and legal line.
